title: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS)
intro: Premenstrual syndrome is a pattern of physical and emotional symptoms that appear in the days before a period and ease once bleeding starts. Many women notice mild changes, while for some the symptoms are severe enough to disturb work and relationships. Lifestyle measures and, if needed, medicines can help.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: Common symptoms include breast tenderness, bloating, headaches, tiredness, food cravings, irritability, low mood, anxiety and difficulty sleeping. Symptoms begin in the second half of the cycle, usually about a week before the period, and disappear within a few days after bleeding begins. A severe form with marked mood symptoms is called premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

sections.heading: Causes
paragraphs: The cause is not fully known. It seems to relate to how the brain responds to normal hormonal fluctuations, involving chemical messengers such as serotonin. It is not caused by weak character, and it is not simply stress. Women with a history of depression, anxiety or high stress may be more affected.

sections.heading: Keeping a symptom diary
paragraphs: Recording symptoms daily for two or more cycles shows whether they follow the typical pattern and helps distinguish PMS from depression, thyroid problems or other conditions that do not improve with the period. It also makes it easier to discuss treatment with your doctor.

sections.heading: What can help
paragraphs: Regular exercise, enough sleep, a balanced diet with less caffeine, salt and alcohol, and relaxation methods can reduce symptoms. Calcium supplements may help some women, and the evidence for other supplements is mixed. Painkillers ease cramps and headaches. Cognitive behavioural therapy is effective for mood symptoms.

sections.heading: Medical treatment
paragraphs: For severe symptoms, antidepressants of the serotonin type taken throughout the cycle or only in the second half can be very effective. Some combined contraceptive pills reduce symptoms, and other hormonal options are available for selected women. Discuss benefits and side effects with your doctor, and review treatment regularly. Seek help urgently if you have thoughts of harming yourself.

examples.title: Tracking the pattern
examples.text: Imagine your mood drops each month before your period. You could rate your symptoms daily for three months and take the chart to your doctor to talk about options.

examples.title: Planning around the cycle
examples.text: Suppose you know the week before your period is hardest. You might avoid scheduling stressful events then, keep up exercise and plan time for rest.
